simple.meaning: חָרִיט (chârîyṭ) is a Hebrew word meaning “properly, cut out (or hollow ), i.e. (by implication) a pocket.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: חָרִיט (H2754) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 2 Kings 5:23, with occurrences in 2 Kings, Isaiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חָרִיט (H2754) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in חָרִיט (H2754) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: חָרִיט (chârîyṭ) / H2754 is traced through 2 Kings 5:23, Isaiah 3:22 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.
